attempts.label: DANDI:001836
attempts.paper_title: Naturalistic behavior and self-generated neural activity predictive of self-correction
attempts.entry_title: Change-of-mind behavior in the spatial sequence task (Gu et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most behavioral findings held: rats learned the sequence, started biased toward side switching, corrected course on change-of-mind trials to the level of run-through trials, and showed fewer ripples during change of mind. The fall in switch bias held only in part (final ratio 1.85, not about 1.5), and the drop in switching on final choices was significant in fewer rats than reported. Distant decoded content was stronger after stopping than before in most rats, but its excess over inbound runs did not hold, and the files do not say which decoder made those tables. Links of remote and local extended content to correct next choices could not be tested because the decoder output is not deposited. Trial counts fell short because the dandiset holds fewer trials.
attempts.description: Tests the behavioral findings of Gu, Liu, Gillespie, Nevers, Denovellis, Coulter, Kay and Frank (2026) on dandiset 001836, which holds the recordings of five rats learning a hidden four-arm sequence. It builds trials from the well pokes and pumps, detects change-of-mind trials on the deposited linearized position, and tests learning, side-switching bias, trial counts and the corrective effect of changes of mind. It reads the paper's triggered decode tables for the Figure 3 claims and detects ripples on the LFP for Figure S7B; the other claims on hippocampal content need the decoder output, which the dandiset does not hold.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gu et al. (2026) from dandiset 001836

outcomes.statement: All rats learned the spatial sequence task over a period of 5 to 19 days, the percentage of consecutive trials conforming to the correct sequence transitions rising over the days analysed.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 4; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: All rats learned the task over a period of 5-19 days (Figure 1B,C, Figure S1E)
outcomes.notes: Per day, the fraction of adjacent-trial transitions that are transitions of the rat's rewarded cycle (sessions with at least 20 trials) rises from 0.268, 0.338, 0.312, 0.416 and 0.408 on the first day to 0.511, 0.629, 0.598, 0.581 and 0.537 on the peak day for rats M, E, J, K and L, all above 0.25. The Spearman correlations with day are 1.00, 0.97, 0.72, 0.67 and 0.77, all positive (p = 0.071 and 0.072 for K and L; the criterion asks only for a positive sign). The peak day is every rat's last day in the dandiset. The dandiset holds 5, 9, 12, 8 and 6 days, against about 6, 9, 11, 8 and 6 in Figure 1C. The rats almost never repeat an arm (52 of 14708 transitions), so chance without repeats is 1/3, not the 25% of the paper and the criterion; the first day is above 1/3 in 3 rats (E, K, L) and the peak day in all 5.
deviations: The rat's cycle is read from the reward log (claims file, opening comment); a reward is followed by a reward at the cycle's next arm in 96 to 100% of cases, and trials are rewarded exactly when the final arm is the cycle's next arm after the last reward in 99.96% of the 14627 trials where that arm is defined.

Trials are built from the digital poke and pump events of the raw files (Methods, Behavioral analysis), a trial running from a home reward to the next outer poke. Against the Statescript logs of rats E, J, K and L the rewarded trials and the trials differ by at most one per session. Rat M's logs hold no counts to compare.

outcomes.statement: The dataset analysed holds 2370, 3554, 4628, 3779 and 2087 trials for rats M, E, J, K and L, of which 107, 225, 138, 315 and 309 are COM trials, hundreds of COM trials per subject.
outcomes.source: Figure 1E inset; Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: In total, we identified hundreds of COM trials per subject (Figure 1E inset
outcomes.notes: Values are reading a-i (10 cm, all trials), the first the criterion lists. Trials are 2083, 3519, 4578, 2959 and 1816 for M, E, J, K and L against 2370, 3554, 4628, 3779 and 2087; COM trials are 120, 196, 126, 226 and 240 against 107, 225, 138, 315 and 309. Within tolerance are 3 of 10 counts under readings a-i and a-ii, and 4 of 10 under b-i and b-ii (0.1 of the 96 cm arm, 9.6 cm; COM 120, 206, 128, 231 and 242), against the 8 the criterion asks for (5 for a partial reproduction). Every rat has at least 120 COM trials under every reading, so the "hundreds of COM trials per subject" part holds in the sense of the criterion. The dandiset holds 0.88, 0.99, 0.99, 0.78 and 0.87 of the paper's trials; the COM share of trials is 0.058, 0.056, 0.028, 0.076 and 0.132 against the paper's 0.045, 0.063, 0.030, 0.083 and 0.148, so for rats K and L most of the shortfall in COM trials follows the shortfall in trials. Per day, rat M has 5 days of 400 to 480 trials against the 6 days the paper reports, which would account for its shortfall; rats K and L have the 8 and 6 days of Figure 1C (319 to 456 trials a day for K, 265 to 337 for L), and no epoch is tagged other than "Session" or "Sleep", so where their missing trials are cannot be told from the files.
deviations: COM detection on the deposited 500 Hz linearization (Methods, Change of mind time detection), whose outer arms are 85.3 to 87.2 cm long in its units, against the 96 cm of the Methods; the 0.1-of-arm reading uses 0.1 of 96 cm (Methods, Behavioral apparatus, "The distance from the beginning of the arm to the end of the reward station is 96 cm"). The binary closing of the reversal mask uses scipy's default structure, as the Methods name the function without parameters.
The claims file's code reading that requires 0.8 s of position in the second before the reversal is applied; the 500 Hz linearization has at most 8% NaN samples in any epoch.

outcomes.statement: Early in learning every rat was biased to side-switching transitions, with a ratio of switch-side to same-side transition probabilities greater than 2 (the ratio for a random choice).
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 4; Figure 1D
outcomes.quote: Initially animals were biased strongly to switch-side transitions (Figure 1D; ratios were greater than 2 for all animals
outcomes.notes: On the first analysed day P(switch-side)/P(same-side) is 5.53, 4.23, 3.76, 2.31 and 2.25 for rats M, E, J, K and L; the mean of the first two days is 5.59, 3.54, 4.00, 2.66 and 2.30. Both readings put all five above 2 (one-sided binomial p = 0.031). Transitions to the same arm (52 of 14708) are neither switch-side nor same-side and are left out.
deviations: Transitions between two trials to the same arm are left out, as they are neither kind; the claims file does not say.

outcomes.statement: As learning progressed the switch-side to same-side ratio fell to about 1.5, with each day in the maze multiplying the bias by an estimated 0.92.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 4; Figure 1D
outcomes.quote: As learning progressed, this ratio decreased to ~1.5 (mixed generalized logistic effect, mean multiplicative estimate of number of days spent in the maze in reducing bias is 0.92, p < 1e-4)

statistics.test: mixed generalized logistic model, effect of days

outcomes.notes: The logistic regression over 14656 transitions gives a day effect of 0.933 (95% CI 0.920 to 0.946, p = 2.3e-23), within 0.92 plus or minus 0.092, the same with the day counted from the first or from the last day and with or without an intercept. The ratio on the peak day is 1.85 as a mean over rats (1.69, 1.94, 1.88, 1.84 and 1.89 for M, E, J, K and L) and 1.84 pooled, both outside 1.5 plus or minus 0.15. Fitted per rat, the day effect is significant in M, E, J and L and not in K (0.984, p = 0.38).
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out, as for fig1c-learning; the claims file does not say whether this claim uses the same selection.

outcomes.statement: In most COM trials the rats changed their minds once (entering two choice arms), but trials with several COM events (more than two arms entered) occurred in every rat.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 5; Figure S1F
outcomes.quote: In most COM trials, rats changed their minds once (entered 2 choice arms), though trials with multiple COM events (>2 arms entered in a trial) were also seen in all rats
outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. With the 10 cm threshold, the share of COM trials with one COM event is 0.875, 0.923, 0.960, 0.888 and 0.891 for M, E, J, K and L, and 15, 15, 5, 25 and 26 trials have two or more events (up to 5 in rat K). Trials with two or more COM arms, more than two arms entered, occur in every rat (14, 15, 5, 24 and 26). The 9.6 cm threshold gives the same outcome.
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.statement: COM trials were corrective; the final choice of a COM trial was rewarded more often than the initial choice would have been, in each rat.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 6; Figure 1G
outcomes.quote: the final decision in COM trials resulted in higher reward rates than would have been the case had the animal continued with their initial choice

statistics.about: rats M, J, K and L

outcomes.notes: Daily medians of the probability that the initial choice would have been rewarded are 0.18, 0.18, 0.00, 0.14 and 0.09 for M, E, J, K and L, and of the final choice being rewarded 0.47, 0.55, 0.72, 0.57 and 0.66; rank-sum p = 0.028, 0.0004, below 1e-4, 0.0008 and 0.0039. The paper reports p < 0.01 for M, J, K and L and p < 0.05 for E; here M is the rat at p < 0.05 only. Two COM trials, first in their session before any reward, have no correct arm and are left out. The 0.1-of-arm threshold (9.6 cm) gives the same outcome. Sessions with at least 20 trials (221 COM trials of rat K).
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.statement: After correction, the reward rate on COM trials did not differ from that of temporally nearby run-through trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 6; Figure 1G
outcomes.quote: These corrections brought the average performance on COM trials up to the level seen on run-through trials
outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. Over 100 draws of nearby non-COM trials, each rat's median rank-sum p is 0.60, 0.57, 0.22, 0.17 and 0.75 for M, E, J, K and L at 10 cm (0.68, 0.52, 0.20, 0.16 and 0.75 at 9.6 cm); the share of draws with p < 0.05 is at most 0.22 (rat K). The median differences of daily reward rate, COM minus nearby, are -0.03, -0.08, 0.12, 0.05 and 0.00. Every COM trial had an eligible nearby trial. Each rat has 5 to 12 daily values, so the test has little power and the result is an absence of evidence.
deviations: Nearby trials are drawn within the same session; the Methods (Identification of nearby trials) say only within plus or minus 3 trials. The random draws use a fixed seed.
Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.statement: The initial choice on COM trials was heavily biased to side-switching, while the final choice was much less so, with a switch-side to same-side ratio close to 1.
outcomes.source: Results, Rat spatial sequence task and change-of-mind behavior, paragraph 7; Figure 1H
outcomes.quote: The initial choice on COM trials was heavily biased to be a side-switch, while the final choice was much less likely to be a side-switch with a ratio of switching to same-side transitions close to 1

statistics.about: initial against final ratio, all rats except M
initial ratio against 2, rats J and K
initial ratio against 2, rats E and L
final ratio against 2, rats J, K, E and L

outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. The mean daily initial ratio exceeds the final in all five rats (medians 3.00 to 3.63 against 0.93 to 1.41), but the paired t-test reaches p < 0.01 only in rats J and K (p = 0.0023 and 0.0045 at 10 cm); E and L have p = 0.013 and 0.014 and M p = 0.42. The 9.6 cm threshold gives the same count (J 0.0022, K 0.0001, E 0.017, L 0.018). The criterion asks for four rats at p < 0.01, or three for a partial reproduction, so the outcome is not reproduced; at p < 0.05 four rats (E, J, K, L) would hold, which is the pattern the legend reports with p < 0.01. The sign tests hold as the legend says at 10 cm, the initial ratio above 2 and the final below 2 with p < 0.05 in E, J, K and L and not in M. Days with no same-side transition are dropped, as the criterion says (1 day of E and 2 of J for the initial ratio). In a variant asked for by the verifier, adding one to both counts so that no day is dropped, J, K and L reach p < 0.01 and E has p = 0.010; that would be a partial reproduction, but the criterion's rule decides.
deviations: The previous trial is the one before in the same session, and transitions from the previous arm to the same arm are left out as neither switch-side nor same-side; the claims file does not say.
Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.statement: The final choice of COM trials did not differ from a switch-side to same-side ratio of 1 in any rat.
outcomes.source: Figure 1H legend
outcomes.quote: between final ratio and 1 yield insignificant difference in all rats
outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. The sign test of the daily final-choice ratios against 1 gives p = 0.38, 0.18, 1.0, 0.45 and 0.22 for M, E, J, K and L, so no rat differs; the median ratios are 1.29, 1.33, 1.00, 0.93 and 1.41. For rat M (5 days) the test cannot reach p < 0.05 (smallest two-sided p 0.0625), so this is a weak absence result there.
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.statement: Before stopping, COM trials showed more extended hippocampal representations within the arm than outbound run-through trials over matched arm regions.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraph 4; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: We found that there were more extended representations preceding stopping on COM trials than run-through trials (Figure 3B, ranksum test, p < 0.01 for all rats)
outcomes.notes: COM rows are the 908 rows of the 160 COM-triggered, arm-restricted tables from arm entry to stopping (in a median 90% of rows per file the trigger lies within 20 ms of one of this entry's COM times, at a median distance of 2 ms); 896 have a distance. Controls are the 975 rows of the 177 tables triggered at the outer poke, 2 s before it (outbound runs), restricted to the arm; 737 have a distance over a head range drawn from the same day's COM rows. Largest |head - decode| at 4 cm/s or more, COM against matched control: medians 13.8 against 10.0 cm (M), 12.7 against 12.5 (E), 15.8 against 13.6 (J), 19.3 against 13.1 (K) and 16.4 against 13.0 (L); one-sided rank-sum p < 1e-4, 0.053, 0.0072, < 1e-4 and < 1e-4. So COM is greater at p < 0.01 in 4 of 5 rats (not E). Only reading (b)(i) can be run: the arm-restricted tables set moments with 0.2 or less of the posterior in the arm to NaN, and the control tables hold only the 2 s before the poke, not 5 s. Without matching the arm range the controls have larger distances (p = 1.0 in all five rats). The arm range of each control row is one random draw, as in the code, and the outcome depends on it. Over 20 further draws, each with its own seed, all five rats hold in 11 draws, four in 8 and three in 1 (E and J each fail in 5), and the median p over the draws is below 0.01 in every rat (E 0.007, J 0.0045). Adding to the COM rows the 48 rows of the arm-restricted tables before stopping that match neither trigger (14 of E, 23 of J), three rats hold in the first draw (E p = 0.088, J 0.013), and over the further draws five rats hold in 3, four in 11 and three in 6 (median p for E 0.014). With all of the paper's COM tables the result is partial in most draws, so the outcome is kept.
deviations: The `scratch/triggered` tables carry no description. They are read with the paper's code, which wrote them (Gu2026 at commit 0f0c9a7, changeOfMind_triggered_position.save_triggered_position_decode_day, changeOfMind_triggered.find_triggered_session and turnaround_triggered_decode), and each file is identified by aligning its trigger times with this entry's COM times (10 cm and 9.6 cm) and outer pokes, by its window, and by whether its positions are relative to the trigger (restricted to the COM arm). The decodes are the MAP (their values lie on the decoder's 2 cm position grid), from the causal posterior as the code reads it. The arm regions are the code's (changeOfMind_remote_interval.loc1d_to_baseoff) and match the arm bases of the deposited linearization.

The control rows are the outbound tables the paper's code wrote (2 s before the outer poke), not trials drawn here; the arm range of each is drawn from the same day's COM rows with a fixed seed (figure4c.return_distance_day).

outcomes.statement: Longer decoded distances before stopping predicted that a trial would have an upcoming COM event, with an odds fold change of 1.06 per unit distance.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: decoded distances were predictive of whether the trial would have an upcoming COM event (Mixed logistic regression, mean multiplicative effect (95% CI) ... 1.06 (1.05, 1.08), p < 1e-20
outcomes.notes: Logistic regression of COM row (1) against matched control row (0) with one indicator per rat: reading (a), distance alone, odds fold change 1.047 per cm (95% CI 1.035 to 1.060, p = 8.5e-14, n = 1633); reading (b), with the speed before stopping, 1.079 (1.062 to 1.096, p = 2.6e-20, n = 1284). Both are within 1.06 plus or minus 0.02, but neither reaches p < 1e-20, so the outcome is partial (above 1 with p < 0.05). Over 20 further draws of the control arm ranges, reading (a) gives 1.042 to 1.056, always within tolerance, with p from 3e-16 to 4e-12; reading (b) gives 1.069 to 1.095, with p below 1e-20 in 13 draws but within tolerance in only 6, and no draw meets both. The partial outcome does not depend on the draw.
deviations: The `scratch/triggered` tables carry no description. They are read with the paper's code, which wrote them (Gu2026 at commit 0f0c9a7, changeOfMind_triggered_position.save_triggered_position_decode_day, changeOfMind_triggered.find_triggered_session and turnaround_triggered_decode), and each file is identified by aligning its trigger times with this entry's COM times (10 cm and 9.6 cm) and outer pokes, by its window, and by whether its positions are relative to the trigger (restricted to the COM arm). The decodes are the MAP (their values lie on the decoder's 2 cm position grid), from the causal posterior as the code reads it. The arm regions are the code's (changeOfMind_remote_interval.loc1d_to_baseoff) and match the arm bases of the deposited linearization.
Rows and distances as in fig3b-extended-before-stopping; speed is the head range over the window divided by its duration, for windows of at least 250 samples (figure4c.make_distance_plot).

outcomes.statement: Representations far from the animal were much more prevalent after stopping than before; before stopping they rarely reached the end of the current arm or other arms.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraphs 4 and 5; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: These more distant representations were much more prevalent following stopping (Figure 3A (b, c), 3C, paired t-test, p < 0.001 for all rats
outcomes.notes: The whole-track tables 5 s either side of COM time (262 files) come in pairs with the same triggers and different decodes; the code runs two decoders (run_time and all_maze) and the files do not say which is which. One member of each pair (decoder A) has the decodes of the arm-restricted tables on the arm (in 157 of the 162 pairs that can be compared, exactly one member agrees on 0.99 or more of the shared samples). Per event both bounds are shown, the decode with the smaller and with the larger post-minus-pre rise, and each decoder. The tables hold 889 events, 829 with both parts. Under the smaller bound, mean largest maze distance before against after stopping is 20.0 against 49.9 cm (M), 23.8 against 43.9 (E), 26.4 against 42.4 (J), 38.9 against 58.1 (K) and 25.3 against 67.0 (L), paired t-test p = 4e-12, 4e-15, 0.10, 2e-11 and 8e-32; under the larger, p < 1e-28 in M, E, K and L and 0.003 in J; under decoder A, p from 1e-13 to 2e-39 in M, E, K and L and 0.058 in J. Post exceeds pre at p < 0.001 in 4 of 5 rats under every bound and decoder. Rat J has 26 events, against 105 COM rows in fig3b, because 34 of its 72 whole-track tables around a trigger match neither trigger. Adding their rows does not change this. With the rows within 20 ms of a COM time of this entry, J has 47 events and p = 0.23 (smaller bound) and 0.048 (decoder A); with all their rows, 52 events and p = 0.19 and 0.037. The other four rats hold in every variant.
deviations: The `scratch/triggered` tables carry no description. They are read with the paper's code, which wrote them (Gu2026 at commit 0f0c9a7, changeOfMind_triggered_position.save_triggered_position_decode_day, changeOfMind_triggered.find_triggered_session and turnaround_triggered_decode), and each file is identified by aligning its trigger times with this entry's COM times (10 cm and 9.6 cm) and outer pokes, by its window, and by whether its positions are relative to the trigger (restricted to the COM arm). The decodes are the MAP (their values lie on the decoder's 2 cm position grid), from the causal posterior as the code reads it. The arm regions are the code's (changeOfMind_remote_interval.loc1d_to_baseoff) and match the arm bases of the deposited linearization.

Maze distance as in figure4c.maze_distance: head within the first 80 cm of the arm at 4 cm/s or more, through the centre when the decode is on another arm, NaN when it is in the centre. Speed is the camera-rate Spyglass head velocity, the paper's head_speed at that rate.

outcomes.statement: After stopping on COM trials, representations reached more distant locations than when animals were at the same locations without a COM, returning from the outer well to the home arm.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraph 5; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: We also found that post-COM representations were more likely to represent distant locations than when animals were in the same location without a COM
outcomes.notes: Post-stopping largest maze distance of the COM events of fig3c-distant-after-stopping against inbound rows, the tables triggered at the outer poke for the 5 s after it, restricted to the arm, over a head range drawn from the same day's COM post-stopping ranges; 296 of 974 inbound rows have positions at 4 cm/s or more in the drawn range. One-sided rank-sum, COM greater: under the smaller decode bound p = 3e-8, 0.041, 0.062, 8e-15 and 8e-9 for M, E, J, K and L (3 rats at p < 0.0001, 4 at p < 0.05, the partial bar); under the larger bound p = 9e-14, 5e-10, 0.008, 7e-20 and 8e-14 (4 rats at p < 0.0001, the full bar). The two-sided variant gives 3 rats at p < 0.0001 under the smaller bound (and 3 at p < 0.05) and 4 under the larger. The outcome verified in round 2 rested on the smaller bound. Round 2 identified the decoder: every arm-restricted table, the inbound ones among them, has the decodes of one decoder (A; 353 pairs of arm-restricted tables sharing samples all agree), and the code takes the COM and control decodes of a figure from one decoder. Under decoder A, p = 2e-8, 0.053, 0.064, 1e-16 and 9e-9 (3 rats at p < 0.0001 and 3 at p < 0.05, below the partial bar). The inbound arm ranges are one random draw per row; over 20 further draws decoder A meets the partial bar in 13 and the full bar in none (median p for E 0.045, J 0.063); the smaller bound meets the partial bar in 17, the larger bound and decoder B the full bar in all 20. Adding the whole-track tables around COM time that match neither trigger, decoder A gives p < 0.05 in 3 rats (E 0.090 with their rows within 20 ms of this entry's COM times, 0.16 with all their rows), and no further draw meets the partial bar under either. Measured within the arm on both sides (the arm-restricted COM tables, the measure of the inbound rows), COM is greater at p < 0.05 in 3 rats (E 0.90, J 0.13), and 3 of 20 further draws meet the partial bar. With the decoder identified and all of the paper's COM tables the claim is not reproduced, as the third verification round agreed. The result is borderline: it rests on the first draw and on counting the tables that match neither trigger as COM tables, which may come from a parameter set the paper did not use for Figure 3D.
deviations: The `scratch/triggered` tables carry no description. They are read with the paper's code, which wrote them (Gu2026 at commit 0f0c9a7, changeOfMind_triggered_position.save_triggered_position_decode_day, changeOfMind_triggered.find_triggered_session and turnaround_triggered_decode), and each file is identified by aligning its trigger times with this entry's COM times (10 cm and 9.6 cm) and outer pokes, by its window, and by whether its positions are relative to the trigger (restricted to the COM arm). The decodes are the MAP (their values lie on the decoder's 2 cm position grid), from the causal posterior as the code reads it. The arm regions are the code's (changeOfMind_remote_interval.loc1d_to_baseoff) and match the arm bases of the deposited linearization.

Assumed in round 2, now replaced: the outcome under the smaller of the two decodes of each event was kept, since the files did not say which decoder made which table and the code uses both (figure4c.get_position_decode_data_day); under the other the claim is reproduced.

Assumed: decoder A, the decoder of every arm-restricted table and so of the inbound rows, since figure4c.get_position_decode_data_day takes the pre, post and control decodes of a figure from one decoder_type. That A is the run_time decoder of the Methods (encoding on spikes at more than 4 cm/s) and of the code's defaults (load_day_decode, maze_distance_animal) is likely but not shown by the files. The COM events are those of every whole-track table around COM time, including those that match neither trigger: the tables classed as COM tables also hold rows at times other than this entry's COM times (a median 23% of rows per file), and the split between them is only this entry's majority rule.

The inbound tables are restricted to the arm, so their maze distance is within the arm, while the COM post-stopping distance uses the whole-track tables, as the code's two inputs do (figure4c.plot_2D_distance_distribution_post reads the COM distances from maze_distance on the whole-track tables). This favours COM; the same within-arm measure on both sides is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Remote arm representations during COM events predicted the immediate next choice (fold change 1.96), but not the last rewarded arm, the last arm chosen or the next correct arm.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives predict correct choices, paragraph 4; Figure 4E
outcomes.quote: We found that remote arm representations were predictive of the immediate next choice (Figure 4E, mixed logistic regression for all rats data, fold change (95% CI), and p-value due to rewarded past, immediate past, correct future, and next choice are 1.07 (0.78,1.50), p < 0.7; 1.16 (0.85,1.59), p < 0.35; 1.31 (0.96, 1.80), p < 0.1; 1.96 (1.45, 2.65), p < 0.0001)

statistics.n: 18, 35, 21, 135 and 93 COM events for rats M, E, J, K and L

outcomes.notes: Remote events need the decoder's posterior per 2 ms bin over each COM event and its continuous-state probability, which the dandiset does not hold; the triggered tables hold only the MAP position in windows around COM times and outer pokes. They would have to be recomputed by spike detection and clusterless state-space decoding of every run session from the 30 kHz voltage, 12.5 TB of raw files over the 40 days (313 GB per day on average); streaming alone at the rate the notebook measures on an LFP file (62 to 72 MB/s over the runs of this revision) would take about 2 days.

outcomes.statement: Remote content also occurred during normal forward running after the animal had turned around, so the jumps are not due to backing up.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraph 6; Figure S6
outcomes.quote: we also observed remote content during normal forward ... running after the animal had turned around but had yet to exit the arm
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4e-next-choice (remote events), blocked as too large.

outcomes.statement: The non-local activity during COM occurred during theta, not during sharp-wave ripples; COM periods had a lower ripple rate, while trial ends, rewarded or not, had higher rates.
outcomes.source: Results, Hippocampal representations of alternatives are only expressed after stopping, paragraph 2; Figure S7B
outcomes.quote: occurred exclusively ... during the hippocampal theta rhythm, which is generally associated with movement
outcomes.notes: Measured values are window a, reading (ii), the first matching reading the criterion lists, without the reference subtraction. SWRs detected on the 1 kHz LFP of 39 days (rat M's fifth day has no LFP file; 64 of 2706 windows dropped). Per rat, as many unrewarded and rewarded trial ends as COM trials (120, 196, 124, 223, 239). Under reading (iii), the pseudo-inverse fit with a constant, all rat indicators and the three conditions, the COM coefficient is negative and both end coefficients positive with p < 0.05 in both windows and both reference readings (window a, no subtraction, -0.043, 0.049 and 0.030 events/s, p = 6e-12, 3e-15 and 1e-6). Reading (ii), z-scored within rat, holds without the subtraction in both windows (window a -0.22, 0.15 and 0.07; the rewarded value is outside 0.30 plus or minus 0.16) and not with it; reading (i), the three conditions without a constant, holds in none. The mean COM rate is below both end rates in 5 of 5 rats in window a without the subtraction and in 4 of 5 otherwise. Ripples are rare: 0.13 to 0.34 per second of immobility in the baseline windows and at most 0.22 per second at trial ends. The LFP shares the behavioral clock: theta amplitude correlates with head speed at no shift (median Spearman 0.68 over 13 days) and not at shifts of 5 or 30 s (-0.20 to -0.02), weakly in rat K. Against the paper's coefficients (-0.18, 0.22 and 0.30), the z-scored reading gives a COM coefficient of larger magnitude and smaller end-of-trial coefficients. With one rat left out, reading (iii) holds in every fit without the subtraction; with the subtraction it holds with any of M, E, J or L left out and fails without rat K (window a, COM -0.0009, p = 0.62; window b, unrewarded end -0.011), so with the subtraction the result rests on rat K, which has no reference channel in its files. The outcome stands on the reading without the subtraction, which holds with any rat left out.
deviations: Ripple band, consensus trace, thresholds and speed limits from the Methods (SWR detection; Electrophysiology). The filter is an equiripple FIR with the Methods' band edges, not ghostipy's design, a standard choice.

Assumed: every tetrode with more than one channel in the LFP file is used, as the electrode table gives no locations and the Methods include "all electrodes with visible SWRs"; the first good channel of each.

Assumed: the corpus callosum reference of the Methods is the channel named by `ref_elect_id` where it is in the file (all days of M, E, J and L, no day of K); the result is shown with and without the subtraction and the outcome is the same.
Assumed: the session baseline (mean and SD at speed above 4 cm/s) is estimated per run epoch from 20 windows of 4 s spread over the epoch, to keep streaming small.

Windows (a) 2 s around COM time and the 2 s after the outer poke, (b) from COM time (stopping) to leaving the arm and from the outer poke to the last beam release at that well before a poke elsewhere; the first COM event of each COM trial; sessions with at least 20 trials; rate as SWR onsets per second of window.

findings.statement: The decoder output behind Figures 4, 5 and S3 to S11 (the posterior per 2 ms bin over whole sessions, the continuous and fragmented state probabilities, the detected remote and local extended events) is not deposited, nor are the spike marks or MUA times. The triggered tables hold only the MAP position in windows around COM times and outer pokes. The rest would have to be recomputed from the raw voltage, 12.5 TB of raw files.

None of the 2415 Spyglass analysis files (`obj-*.nwb`) says what it holds; the file names carry only an object id, and their tables have empty descriptions. By content they are head position, velocity and orientation (750), linearized position at about 23 Hz and at 500 Hz (446), and decodes triggered on events (1219). The triggered tables could be read only with the paper's code and by aligning their trigger times with COM times and outer pokes: 720 are triggered at COM times, 353 at outer pokes, and 146 at times that match neither. The parameters that made each (trigger, window, restriction to the arm, MAP or mean, which decoder) are in the lab's database, not the files; the whole-track tables come in pairs with different decodes, and which decoder made each can be told only from which member agrees with the arm-restricted tables, not named. The track graph of the linearization is not deposited.

The dandiset holds fewer trials than the paper reports for three rats. Built from the poke and pump events, it holds 2083, 3519, 4578, 2959 and 1816 trials for rats M, E, J, K and L, against 2370, 3554, 4628, 3779 and 2087 in the Figure 1E inset (0.88, 0.99, 0.99, 0.78 and 0.87 of them). Rat M has 5 days against the 6 the paper says were collected; rat J has 12 days against about 11 in Figure 1C. Rat M's 5 days of about 400 trials would account for its shortfall; rats K and L have the days of Figure 1C, and no epoch is tagged other than Session or Sleep, so where their trials are missing is not known.
Rat M's 500 Hz linearizations are each deposited twice, in 26 pairs of files with identical values, one pair per run epoch. They are counted once.

Rat M's Statescript logs are named "syayescript Seq2Session1" and so on, a misspelling of "statescript", and hold no trial or reward counts, unlike the other rats' logs. Rat M's days also have 4 LFP files for 5 days.

The reward log gives the cycle 3-4-2-1-3 for rats M, E and J and 1-2-4-3-1 for rats K and L. This fits the Results (1-2-4-3-1 in 2 rats, 3-4-2-1-3 in 3) and the Figure 1B legend (rat E, 3-4-2-1-3), while Figure S1E labels Seq2 (1-2-4-3-1) for M, E and J. The files name the epochs of K and L "Rev2" and those of M, E and J "Seq2".
The head orientation series (`scratch/CompassDirection/head_orientation`) gives its unit as meters.

The electrode table of the LFP files has no locations, so the CA1 tetrodes and the corpus callosum reference used for ripple detection (Methods, SWR detection) cannot be identified; the reference named by `ref_elect_id` is in the LFP file on some days only (never for rat K).
The LFP series (`scratch/filtered data`) gives its unit as volts with a conversion of 1.0, while the data are int16 values with a standard deviation of about 240.

For Figure 3D, which decoder (run_time or all_maze) made the whole-track tables the paper used, and which made the arm-restricted tables? The deposited whole-track tables come in pairs with different decodes; one member of each pair (A) agrees with every arm-restricted table. Under A the claim is at the edge of its partial bar (3 or 4 rats at p < 0.05 depending on the random draw of arm ranges), under the other decoder it holds in full (4 rats at p < 0.0001). Which tables around COM time entered Figure 3 (146 tables have rows mostly not at this attempt''s COM times) is also not said.

For Figure S7B, which tetrodes and which reference channel entered SWR detection, and over what period was the session baseline taken? This attempt used every tetrode of the LFP file, the `ref_elect_id` channel where present or none, and 20 sampled windows per run epoch; ripples came out rare (0.13 to 0.34 per second of immobility).

entries.name: 001836-gu-2026
entries.title: Change-of-mind behavior in the spatial sequence task (Gu et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the behavioral findings of Gu, Liu, Gillespie, Nevers, Denovellis, Coulter, Kay and Frank (2026) on dandiset 001836, which holds the recordings of five rats learning a hidden four-arm sequence. It builds trials from the well pokes and pumps, detects change-of-mind trials on the deposited linearized position, and tests learning, side-switching bias, trial counts and the corrective effect of changes of mind. It reads the paper's triggered decode tables for the Figure 3 claims and detects ripples on the LFP for Figure S7B; the other claims on hippocampal content need the decoder output, which the dandiset does not hold.
